fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so responding units can pull forward and exit without reversing.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive so fire and rescue vehicles can pass without obstruction on either side.
• Cut back dense vegetation that crowds the area between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation near the structures to create open ground that allows responders to work around the buildings without pushing through heavy brush.
• Post the property address at the street entrance so it is readable at night and from a moving vehicle.
• Identify and communicate the single access point limitation to your local fire station so crews are aware before an incident occurs.
• Keep a clear path along at least one side of the main residence connecting the front yard to the rear so responders are not blocked from reaching the back of the structure.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly against or touching the structure on all sides.
• Trim branches from scattered trees that hang over or reach toward the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation growing close to the base of the structure.
• Cut back shrubs and tall grasses along both sides of the driveway to keep the travel lane open.
• Trim tree branches that overhang the driveway so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation along the driveway that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs in open terrain areas between tree clusters and the structure to reduce connected patches of vegetation.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the rear of the property to open up movement around the back of the structure.
• Keep the single driveway access route free of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and other obstructions year-round.
• Separate tree clusters from each other by removing smaller trees or shrubs growing between them near the structure.
• Remove dead branches and dry plant material from the base of trees surrounding the structure.
